Aforetime
uh-FOR-tyme
adverb
A compound of afore (Old English onforan, “before, in front of”) and time; hence formerly, in time past, in former days — that which was done or written before the present hour.

Biblical Definition

Aforetime means formerly, in time past — and the word is never a mere date. It carries the weight of what went before into what is now. Isaiah recalls a nation’s history to steady it in its present distress: “My people went down aforetime into Egypt to sojourn there; and the Assyrian oppressed them without cause” (Isa 52:4). The God who brought them out of the one house of bondage will bring them out of the other; the past is the pledge. In Daniel the word measures a man’s spine: when the writing was signed and the lions’ den was law, Daniel went home, opened his windows toward Jerusalem, and kneeled three times a day “as he did aforetime” (Dan 6:10). He did not add a prayer for the crisis nor subtract one for the danger — he did what he had always done. That is what habit is for: the settled practice of ordinary days is the only thing that stands up on the day the decree is signed. John names a healed man simply as him “that aforetime was blind” (Joh 9:13) — a whole biography in one adverb, the old life named and left. And Paul makes the word a doctrine of Scripture: “whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope” (Rom 15:4). The Old Testament is not an archive but a schoolroom. What was written aforetime was written for us, and hope is the thing it teaches.

Webster 1828 Definition

In time past; formerly; in former days — that which was done or written before the present hour.

expand to see more

AFORETIME, in time past; in a former time; formerly.

A compound of afore, “before,” and time.

Daniel prayed toward Jerusalem as he did aforetime (Dan 6:10).

The healed man is named him that aforetime was blind (Joh 9:13).

Whatsoever was written aforetime was written for our learning (Rom 15:4).

Key Scripture

Isa 52:4 — "For thus saith the Lord GOD, My people went down aforetime into Egypt to sojourn there; and the Assyrian oppressed them without cause."

Dan 6:10 — "Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime."

Joh 9:13 — "They brought to the Pharisees him that aforetime was blind."

Rom 15:4 — "For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope."

Modern Corruption

A live misuse: the age despises what was written aforetime as merely ancient, and so throws away the schoolroom God gave His church for hope.

expand to see more

Here is a corruption worth naming. Our generation holds a settled contempt for the past — the assumption that what is older is thereby outgrown, that the fathers were simply mistaken about what we have lately discovered, and that a text written aforetime can bind no one now. The academy dresses this up as method, treating the Old Testament as the fossil of a religion rather than the word of the living God; the church absorbs the mood without the argument and quietly stops reading it. Paul says the opposite in one flat sentence: whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning. Not for the archivist. For us. And the fruit of that learning is not information but hope.

The remedy Daniel shows is habit. When the writing was signed and prayer was made a capital crime, he went home, opened the windows toward Jerusalem, and kneeled three times a day “as he did aforetime” — changing nothing, because there was nothing to change. Courage on the day of the decree is only the overflow of obedience on the thousand days before it. The man who prays only in crisis will not pray in the lions’ den. So too the healed man of John 9, named forever as him that aforetime was blind: the past is not erased by grace but transfigured by it, kept as the dark backdrop against which the mercy shows. Despise the aforetime and you lose the learning, the hope, the habit, and the testimony together.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word means formerly, in time past — what was done or written before the present hour.

expand to see more

Aforetime — a compound of afore and time.

From Old English onforan, “before, in front of.”

It denotes former days, the settled past behind the present hour.

Daniel kneeled and prayed as he did aforetime, decree or no decree (Dan 6:10).

What was written aforetime was written for our learning and hope (Rom 15:4).

Usage

"Daniel prayed as he did aforetime: the habit of ordinary days is what stands on the day of the decree."

"Whatsoever was written aforetime was written for our learning — the Old Testament is a schoolroom."

"He that aforetime was blind: grace does not erase the old life, it makes the mercy visible against it."
